description: Population distribution parameters and evidence weights for acoustic voice-sex classification. Each feature is modelled as a Gaussian under each class; evidence is the log-likelihood ratio ln[N(x|F)/N(x|M)]. Weights sum to 1.00 and encode each cue's discriminative reliability (roughly monotonic in d-prime, discounted for content-dependence and measurement fragility).

combination.note: S = sum(w_i * LLR_i) / sum(w_i over AVAILABLE features). Renormalisation over available features keeps the score on a fixed scale when cues are missing (e.g. F4 lost to narrowband audio). A plain naive-Bayes sum would over-count because acoustic cues are correlated (F0 and formants both track androgenisation); a weighted mean under-counts. The gain k below restores calibration and is the single parameter to fit on labelled data.
combination.clamp_note: Per-feature LLR is clamped to +/-6 so one wild measurement (an octave-doubled F0, a spurious LPC root) cannot dominate the verdict.

f0_mean_log.transform: natural log of mean F0 over voiced frames
f0_mean_log.meaning: Rate of vocal-fold vibration. Post-pubertal androgen exposure lengthens folds (M 17-25 mm vs F 12.5-17.5 mm) and adds mass; heavier, longer folds oscillate slower. Modelled in log space because F0 is log-normal and perceptually logarithmic.
f0_mean_log.caveats: Single strongest cue but distributions overlap at 160-190 Hz. Octave errors in the tracker are the most common source of catastrophic misclassification - always cross-check against the formant block.

f0_p5_log.transform: natural log of 5th percentile of voiced F0
f0_p5_log.meaning: Pitch floor - the bottom of the speaker's habitual range, reached at phrase-final falls. Nearly impossible to fake downward and less affected by emotional arousal than the mean.
f0_p5_log.caveats: Corrupted by creak/vocal fry, which drops F0 to 40-70 Hz in both sexes. Discard frames flagged as creak before computing.

vtl_estimate.transform: weighted median of per-formant uniform-tube estimates L_n = (2n-1)c/(4*F_n), c = 35000 cm/s, weights [0.10, 0.20, 0.35, 0.35] for F1..F4
vtl_estimate.meaning: Estimated length of the vocal tract, in centimetres. The single most anatomically direct measurement in the set and, after F0, the strongest discriminator (d' 2.94). Every formant independently implies a tube length; pooling them by weighted median rejects the outlier a single mis-tracked formant would otherwise introduce.
vtl_estimate.caveats: Supersedes the earlier (F4-F1)/3 dispersion statistic, which inherited all of F1's unreliability: F1 is both vowel-dependent and biased low at high F0, where sparse harmonics leave LPC fitting harmonic peaks rather than the true resonance. F1 is retained here at only 0.10 weight for that reason. Requires at least two formants; a wide spread across per-formant estimates signals a tracking failure and trips the inconsistency gate.

f3.meaning: Third vocal-tract resonance. Chosen over F1/F2 because it is largely fixed by tract length rather than by tongue position, so it reports anatomy rather than vowel identity.
f3.caveats: Rhotic /r/ collapses F3 dramatically in both sexes. In heavily rhotic English, downweight or exclude frames with F3 < 2000 Hz.

f4.meaning: Fourth resonance - the most tract-length-determined and least articulation-determined formant we can measure reliably.
f4.caveats: Lost entirely on 8 kHz telephony (Nyquist 4 kHz). The pipeline drops it and redistributes weight rather than reporting a fabricated value.

f1.meaning: First resonance, inversely related to tongue height. Carries genuine tract-length information but is dominated by which vowel is being spoken.
f1.caveats: Deliberately low weight: the vowel /i/ in a male voice can produce a lower F1 than /a/ in a female voice. Content-dependence makes it near-useless on short clips.

f2.meaning: Second resonance, tracks tongue front/back position.
f2.caveats: Same content-dependence problem as F1; weighted accordingly.

h1_h2.transform: amplitude of 1st harmonic minus amplitude of 2nd, in dB
h1_h2.meaning: Open quotient of the glottal cycle - operationally, breathiness. Adult female phonation commonly exhibits a posterior glottal chink (incomplete closure at the rear of the folds during vibration), producing turbulent leakage and disproportionate energy in the first harmonic. Physiologically independent of both F0 and tract length, which is why it earns the highest weight in Tier 2: it carries information the pitch and resonance blocks do not.
h1_h2.caveats: Sensitive to recording channel and low-frequency roll-off. Unusable below ~120 Hz on narrowband audio where H1 falls near the passband edge.

hnr.meaning: Harmonics-to-noise ratio - periodic energy over aperiodic energy. The corroborating half of the breathiness signal.
hnr.caveats: Weak on its own (d' 0.61) and heavily confounded by recording SNR: a noisy male recording mimics a breathy female one. Weight is automatically driven toward zero when the estimated SNR is poor.

jitter_local.meaning: Cycle-to-cycle variation in period length - micro-instability of fold vibration.
jitter_local.caveats: Barely discriminative for sex (it is a clinical marker of pathology, not of anatomy). Included for completeness and diagnostics, weighted near zero by design.

shimmer_local.caveats: As jitter: retained for the record, not for the verdict.

spectral_centroid.meaning: Centre of spectral mass - the physical correlate of perceived brightness. A coarse summary of the same tract-length effect the formants measure precisely.
spectral_centroid.caveats: Strongly affected by microphone response and any EQ applied to the recording.

spectral_rolloff85.meaning: Frequency below which 85 percent of spectral energy lies.
spectral_rolloff85.caveats: Determined as much by the codec and the recording bandwidth as by the speaker. Low weight is deliberate.

unscored_diagnostics.note: Recorded in every report and read by the analyst for corroboration, but NOT given numeric weight. There is no defensible population prior for these without a fitted model, and inventing one would manufacture false confidence.

tier_weight_totals.design_note: Resonance outweighs pitch (0.46 vs 0.34) deliberately, which is the single most consequential choice in this table. Pitch is the more separable cue in isolation, but it is also the cue that is trainable, performable and deliberately modifiable, and the one that fails inside the 160-190 Hz overlap band. Tract length is not volitionally alterable. Weighting resonance above pitch is what prevents the classic failure mode of a high-pitched male or low-pitched female voice being confidently misread. Revision 1.1 replaces raw formant dispersion with a pooled vocal-tract-length estimate at the same 0.20 weight, raising that cue's d' from 1.89 to 2.94 by discounting the least reliable formant instead of averaging it in at full strength.
